chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Musa (peace be upon him) entered ihram from Ramla in Egypt. He said: And he passed through the glens of al-Rawha in a state of ihram, leading his she-camel with a halter made of palm fiber, wearing upon him two Qatwani cloaks, reciting the talbiyya while the mountains responded to him.

key_terms.إحرام: ihram — the sacred state of ritual consecration entered by the pilgrim, marked by special dress and restrictions
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: talbiyya — the pilgrim's chant 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' ('Here I am, O God, here I am')
key_terms.خِطَام: khitam — a camel halter used for guiding
key_terms.رَمْلَة مِصْر: Ramla of Egypt — the sandy/desert region of Egypt from which Musa began his pilgrimage
key_terms.صِفَاح الرَّوْحَاء: Sifah al-Rawha — the broad flat valleys of al-Rawha, on the route between Mecca and Medina
key_terms.عَبَاءَة قَطَوَانِيَّة: Qatwani abaya — a type of woolen cloak associated with the region of Qatwan
key_terms.لِيف: lif — palm fiber; symbolizes humble simplicity

ai.seo_question: Did Prophet Musa (Moses) perform Hajj according to Shia hadith in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS) via a chain reaching al-Kulayni, recounts that the Prophet Musa (Moses, peace be upon him) performed Hajj, beginning his ihram from the sandy lands of Egypt and traveling through the region of al-Rawha near Medina. The description emphasizes his simplicity and humility: his camel was guided by a humble palm-fiber rope, and he wore plain woolen Qatwani garments. The miraculous detail that the mountains echoed his talbiyya underscores the prophetic dignity of his pilgrimage, and the hadith teaches that the rites of Hajj have deep roots across prophetic history predating Islam.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Musaas adorned the Ihraam from Ramla in Egypt, and heas passed by the glens of Al-Rawha wearing Ihraam, sitting on a she-camel harnessed from fibres. Upon himas were two Qatwany cloaks, exclaiming Talbiyya , and the mountains responded to himas’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Moses, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, dressed himself up for Ihram (one of the acts for Hajj) at Ramlah of Misr, (name of a city).’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘He passed over the hillsides of al-Rawha’ on his way to Makkah, in the state of Ihram, driving his camel with a harness made of fiber and having two gowns made in Qatwan, saying, “Here I am O Lord, to obey Your command,” and the hills joined him to say what he said.’”
